title: Split and Merge Array Transformation
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, you can perform split-and-merge operations on nums1.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, you can perform split-and-merge operations on nums1. These operations involve removing a subarray, then re-inserting it at any position. Determine the least number of such operations required to convert nums1 into nums2.
constraints: Both arrays have equal length between two and six.
nums2 is a permutation of nums1, including duplicate multiplicities.
One move removes any contiguous block and reinserts it unchanged anywhere.
hints: The length-six limit makes the finite permutation state graph small enough for BFS.
Treat each distinct array arrangement as a node and every block removal/reinsertion as one edge.
Generate all left/right blocks and insertion positions, deduplicate states, and stop when the target is dequeued.
All legal operations are unit-weight edges, so BFS depth is the minimum number of split-and-merge moves.
editorial: All legal operations are unit-weight edges, so BFS depth is the minimum number of split-and-merge moves.

tests.explanation: Move the leading three to the end in one operation.
Three block moves are necessary and sufficient.
